clue.text: Draw into pub where there are shops etc?

indicators.note: the clue says draw goes into the pub, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
to draw a cart is to tow it

explanation.surface: A suggestion to tempt someone into a pub near the shopping streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like an invitation or a tie, but it means TOW, which goes 'into' INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the centre of a town puts you among the shops, offices and other amenities; the question mark flags this descriptive definition.

clue.text: Dodgy moment after the leader's been deposed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and deposing it removes that letter

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: Things become dodgy for a while after a country's ruler is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' and 'deposed' paint a political coup, but they simply strip the J from the front of JIFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or suspect, the same as dodgy.

clue.text: Old PM, drunk, knocked over seat? Act done carelessly! He must be rare hearty fouling up lines on stage

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the pair of words from the bottom up

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a nineteenth-century British Prime Minister
a sot is a drunkard
a perch is a seat, especially for a bird

indicators.note: a thing done carelessly is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
fouling up means messing up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy former Prime Minister knocks over a chair and is told off by an actor who keeps garbling a famous speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns PEEL plus SOT to give the first two words. 'carelessly' rearranges ACT DONE into ANCE TO D, finishing PERCHANCE TO D; 'fouling up' rearranges the last six words into REAM AY THERE'S THE RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous line from Hamlet's soliloquy, so it is literally lines spoken on stage.

clue.text: Bore should keep quiet about what Iraq seems to have lacked!

definitions.text: what Iraq seems to have lacked!

indicators.note: one word keeping others holds them inside it

parts.note: to weary someone is to bore them
p, for piano, is the musical direction for quiet
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A dull speaker is told to stop going on about the absence of weapons in Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: This refers to the 2003 invasion of Iraq, justified by weapons of mass destruction that were never found.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry means arms in general, and Iraq's supposed arsenal of banned arms turned out not to exist.

clue.text: Avoid terrible pest over the course of fateful day

indicators.note: one thing spread over the course of another wraps right round it
something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was assassinated

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge a nasty pest throughout an ill-omened day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns PEST into S...TEP, which spreads 'over the course of' IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to avoid it, as a dancer or boxer steps aside.

clue.text: I do wrong upsetting the person who needles me — I just want to get my own back!

definitions.text: I just want to get my own back!

indicators.note: upsetting tips something over, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to err is to do wrong
a dentist gives injections, sticking needles into a patient

explanation.surface: A guilty confession about getting revenge on the person who torments me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns ERR to RRE. The definition is a typical speech of someone seeking lost territory, not a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: An irredentist demands the return of territory once held by their nation, wanting their own land back.

clue.text: Furnishes Head of Entertainment with jokes

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: quips are jokes

explanation.surface: A TV boss provides a show with gags.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip a place is to furnish or supply it with what it needs.

clue.text: See 2
See 2
Like celebration heartlessly wild across the street

indicators.note: one word lying across another spans it, so it holds the other inside
losing its heart means a word loses its middle letter

parts.note: feral means wild

explanation.surface: A party that has gone wild and spilled across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle R out of FERAL to give FEAL, which goes 'across' ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Festal is a formal adjective for things belonging to a feast or festival.

clue.text: Fail to collect runs with ball keeping low

indicators.note: collecting something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to go under is to fail, as a business does
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder fails to gather the runs while the ball stays low.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, but GO UNDER is the business sense of failing; R for runs is a scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounder is a ball hit or bowled so that it runs along the ground, staying low.

clue.text: Cheerer stopped getting excited — no words coming directly

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan in the crowd stopped shouting as things heated up.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect speech reports what was said without quoting the speaker's actual words.

clue.text: Old right-winger gives yon revolutionary service

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, pointing at something over there
Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary
a rite is a religious service

explanation.surface: An old Tory hands a rebel's church ceremony to that person over there.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of Margaret Thatcher, the Conservative leader of the 1980s, was a right-winger of a past era.

clue.text: Smart when beset by a soreness — bit of salve is appropriate

indicators.note: a thing beset by others is surrounded by them, so it goes inside

parts.note: pain is soreness
pert means smart or cheeky

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A stinging sore needs a little ointment applied to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like the stinging verb, but it is PERT, beset by A PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain is to belong or be fitting, so it means being appropriate.

clue.text: Girl band given a special day in the calendar?

definitions.meaning: the name of a British pop group of four women, famous around 2000

definitions.text: a special day in the calendar?
definitions.meaning: the first of November is the church feast honouring every saint

explanation.surface: A pop group gets its own date on the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the 1990s British girl group and to the November feast day of the church.

clue.text: Writing on the wall round gents

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
gents are men

explanation.surface: Graffiti scrawled around the gents' toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing on the wall' suggests graffiti in a toilet, but it is the Biblical warning sign of doom.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing on the wall is an idiom for a sign of coming disaster, which is a portent.

clue.text: Be too unemotional maybe, contriving heartlessly cold nature

indicators.note: contriving means devising afresh, so these letters are rearranged
losing its heart means the word cold loses its middle letters

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted person may seem too unfeeling, artfully hiding their true nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' cuts COLD to CD; 'contriving' rearranges CD with NATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To underact is to play a part with too little emotion; 'maybe' marks it as one way of being unemotional.

clue.text: Want servant you rejected to be dismissed

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: a lackey is a servant

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for you is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: A servant you don't want is to be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns YE into EY, and 'to be dismissed' takes EY off the end of LACKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to lack it, as in 'for want of a nail'.

clue.text: Camp bed overlooking lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A campsite with a bed set up looking out over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' reads as a campsite, but it is a clique or faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group, just as a camp is a group sharing a cause.

clue.text: Likely to provoke legal proceedings in a court — one with bail broken

indicators.note: broken things are smashed apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone breaking bail in court is likely to face a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ONE and BAIL into IONABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something actionable gives grounds for a lawsuit, so it could lead to legal action.

clue.text: Zero cloud cover is still theoretical

definitions.meaning: a cloudless day shows nothing overhead but clear blue
used of research or thinking not tied to practical use

explanation.surface: A clear day remains merely hypothetical.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudless sky is literally blue, and blue-sky research is speculative and theoretical.

clue.text: Counter is part of chemist's equipment

definitions.meaning: to counter is to answer back sharply
a glass vessel with a long bent neck used for distilling

explanation.surface: A shop counter forms part of a pharmacy's fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' and 'chemist' suggest a British pharmacy, but the chemist is a scientist in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply countering a remark, and also a distillation flask.

clue.text: See 2
Philosopher is always right

parts.note: aye is an old word meaning always or forever

explanation.surface: A thinker who is never wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Ayer was a twentieth-century British philosopher known for logical positivism.

clue.text: Drug given name — very cold round object swallowed

indicators.note: something swallowed is taken inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold
a round object is the letter O

explanation.surface: A named drug taken with an ice-cold pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' puts O inside ARCTIC; 'round' belongs to the object, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, such as opium.

clue.text: Great fictional character has guns near

parts.note: gat is old American slang for a gun
by means near, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: A notable figure from a novel carries guns close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' is part of the definition: the hero of Fitzgerald's novel is The Great Gatsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the title character of F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby.

clue.text: Covered building retains warmth

indicators.note: a word that retains another holds it inside

parts.note: a shed is a simple building
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A roofed structure keeps the heat in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathed means encased or covered, as a sword in its scabbard.

clue.text: What's brilliant about the old horse? It has stamina

indicators.note: one word about another surrounds it

parts.note: a star is brilliant, shining brightly
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Asking what is so special about an aged horse, and answering that it lasts the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' looks like it describes the horse, but it gives YE, the old form of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a racehorse or runner with the endurance for long distances.
